sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 34.8% a year, from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5.93 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].
Growth stalled in FY2023 at 0.1%, after 64.2% in FY2021 [D311][D218].
The FY2017 operating loss of $3.49 billion reflected stock-based compensation of $2.64 billion, which the filing ties to the CEO award and IPO-triggered RSUs [F12][X82][P74].
Operating margin improved from -30.4% in FY2023 to -9.0% in FY2025, a 5.7pp gain in the latest year [F28][F30][D419].
Other Revenue contributed 5.4pp of FY2025 growth, level with Advertising Revenue's 5.3pp, even though it was only 12.6% of revenue [D545][D538][D543].
The filing attributes the $287.6 million rise in other revenue mainly to subscription growth from more subscribers [P24][S42].
Advertising revenue grew 5.8% as impressions rose about 17%, partly offset by roughly 10% lower cost per impression [D537][P24].
Advertising's share of revenue fell from 95.7% in FY2023 to 87.4% in FY2025 [D532][D536].
Operating leverage is positive: FY2025 revenue growth beat operating-cost growth by 5.5pp, and the incremental operating margin was 44.8% [D430][D429].
FY2025 operating margin of -9.0% is the window high, against a median of -32.4% and a low of -422.5% [F30][D554][D555][D553].
In the FY2025 bridge, other lines added 3.3pp, R&D 1.3pp and cost of revenue 1.1pp; sales and marketing fell $42.4 million on event timing and lower advertising [D433][D432][D431][P22].
The largest annual gain was FY2018's 315.1pp, with R&D adding 120.6pp; the filing cites a $2.1 billion fall in stock-based compensation [D92][D104][P75].
The FY2025 net margin of -7.8% is flattered by a $68.9 million other-income line that included debt-extinguishment gains, while interest expense rose to $122.0 million [F50][X130][P18][X100][P19].
FY2025 operating cash flow of $656.2 million and free cash flow of $437.2 million contrast with a $460.5 million net loss [F80][F100][F40].
The filing says operating cash flow came from the net loss adjusted for non-cash items, including stock-based compensation of $1.0 billion [F80][P13][X90].
Free cash flow margin reached 7.4%, the window high, versus a window median of -4.1% [D393][D560][D561].
Capex of $219.0 million was 3.7% of revenue and 1.34x D&A, mainly leased-facility improvements [F90][D392][D395][P10].
Net debt was $596.3 million in FY2025, against net cash of $1.44 billion in FY2021 [D399][D211].
Net cash was -10.1% of revenue versus a peer median of 45.0%, the 0th percentile among five internet peers [D400][D579][D578].
Cash and investments of $2.94 billion trail total debt of $3.54 billion, and the current ratio of 3.56x is the window low [D397][D398][F180][D565].
Buybacks of $751 million were 171.7% of free cash flow, yet diluted shares still rose 2.1% [X156][D402][D425].
Net losses ran for all ten years, with $460.5 million in FY2025, though the loss narrowed 34.0% that year [R1][F40][D408].
Stock-based compensation was 17.1% of revenue and 191.1% of the operating loss in FY2025, and at least 10% of revenue in nine years [R2][D390][D404].
Net cash has fallen four years running into net debt, while interest expense rose from $21.6 million to $122.0 million on the 2033 and 2034 Notes [R3][D399][X99][X100][P19].
Buybacks exceeded free cash flow in FY2023 to FY2025, at 142.3% in FY2024 and 171.7% in FY2025 [R4][D354][D402].
Free cash flow margin staying at or above the FY2025 level of 7.4% would confirm the conversion trend; a lower print in the FY2026 10-K would reverse it [D393].
Operating margin improving beyond -9.0%, with incremental margin holding near 44.8%, would confirm operating leverage in the FY2026 10-K [F30][D429].
Net debt widening beyond $596.3 million in the FY2026 10-K would signal that buybacks, which were $750.9 million in FY2025, continue to outrun cash generation [D399][X156].
